template:
Hi,

Noticed you do {{business_type}} around {{city}}.

We can book you 10 qualified {{inspection_type}} that turn into paid {{project_type}} jobs, in under 30 days.

You only pay when I book you a qualified, confirmed {{inspection_singular}}.

Open to a 15-minute chat?

instructions.business_type: the trade this company leads with on its own website, lowercase, EXACTLY one of: underpinning, restumping, reblocking, foundation repair, house levelling, slab lifting, house raising. Use the one the site LEADS with (hero line, page title, the first service listed), not one of many further down. Map what the site actually says onto the seven: underpinning / piering / screw piles / mass concrete underpinning / resin injection underpinning -> underpinning; restumping / re-stumping / stump replacement / steel stumps / concrete stumps -> restumping; reblocking / re-blocking -> reblocking (use it only when the site itself says reblocking; a site that says both restumping and reblocking is restumping); foundation repair / footing repair / subsidence repair / foundation cracks / crack repair / ground stabilisation / geopolymer -> foundation repair; house levelling / relevelling / re-levelling / floor levelling / house re-levelling -> house levelling; slab lifting / slab jacking / concrete lifting / concrete levelling / driveway levelling / polyurethane injection under slabs -> slab lifting; house raising / house lifting / raise and build under / house relocation with raising -> house raising. Never any other phrase.
instructions.inspection_type: the FIRST VISIT to a homeowner, plural, in Australian usage: the trade noun for business_type plus that trade's visit word. Take it from this table and change nothing else. underpinning -> site inspections; restumping -> subfloor inspections; reblocking -> subfloor inspections; foundation repair -> foundation inspections; house levelling -> site assessments; slab lifting -> concrete assessments; house raising -> site inspections. If this company's own site consistently calls the first visit something else from the same family ('inspection', 'site inspection', 'assessment', 'site assessment', 'on-site assessment'), use the company's word and keep the trade noun from the table. NEVER the word 'survey' or 'surveys' — an Australian homeowner books an inspection, not a survey. NEVER the word 'free'. NEVER 'estimate' or 'quote'. NEVER the whole business_type phrase inside this value.
instructions.inspection_singular: the singular of inspection_type, from the same table: site inspection, subfloor inspection (restumping and reblocking both), foundation inspection, site assessment, concrete assessment. It reads after 'a qualified, confirmed', so it must be one thing a homeowner books.
instructions.project_type: the OUTCOME NOUN the homeowner pays for, singular, homeowner wording, reading immediately before the word 'jobs'. By business_type: underpinning -> underpinning; restumping -> restumping; reblocking -> reblocking; foundation repair -> rectification; house levelling -> levelling; slab lifting -> relevelling; house raising -> house raising. Never plural. Never a technical or trade-supplier term (say repair, not stabilisation; say relevelling, not 'polyurethane injection'). Never 'project' or 'installation'.
instructions.city: ONLY if the 'city' known fact is blank: the town or suburb this company is based in, read from the website. For a business in a capital-city metro that serves the whole metro, give the CITY ('Sydney', 'Melbourne', 'Brisbane', 'Perth', 'Adelaide', 'Hobart', 'Canberra', 'Darwin'); for a single-suburb or regional business give the TOWN or SUBURB ('Toowoomba', 'Geelong', 'Penrith'). NEVER a state or its abbreviation ('NSW', 'Victoria'), never a region ('South East Queensland', 'the Hunter', 'the Mornington Peninsula') and never a service-area phrase ('servicing Sydney and the Central Coast'). Use a region name ONLY when the site names no town or city at all. Otherwise repeat the known city exactly, with no trailing token of any kind.

rules: Decide business_type first — EXACTLY one of the seven allowed Australian trades, the one the site leads with — then derive inspection_type, inspection_singular and project_type from the per-trade tables above; do not invent an eighth combination. The three trade values must agree with each other: business_type names the trade once, inspection_type is the first visit, project_type is the outcome the homeowner buys. No single word may appear in ALL THREE of business_type, inspection_type and project_type, and inspection_type must never contain the whole business_type phrase — those two are what `fill` reports as flag_word_used_3x and flag_visit_repeats_trade, and a flagged row is re-done. Never the word 'free' anywhere in inspection_type. Australian spelling (levelling, stabilisation) and Australian vocabulary throughout. A restumping firm does not get 'underpinning' because the word appears somewhere on its site, and no company gets 'waterproofing' or 'damp proofing'.

_r._: OPERATOR NOTES — not instructions to the personalisation subagent. They explain why each Australian value differs from personalize-config-uk.json and what to watch in the fill report. DRAFT until the 3-lead and 7-lead wording tests are signed off.
_r.filename: Named personalize-au-config.json (not personalize-config-au.json) so it matches the .gitignore allow pattern `clients/*/*-config.json` and tracks normally without a force-add. build-plusvibe.js takes the path on --config, so the name is free.
_r.template: Identical to the UK template. Australian English uses the same register as UK English for this line ('Noticed you do X around <town>' is how an Australian tradie would say it too), and the UK offer line was approved by the operator on 2026-09-17. No new placeholder: the second-email `company_short` variable is still an open item in STATE.md.
_r.business_type: The seven values are the Australian trade vocabulary from ICP-au.md, not the UK or US lists. 'foundation repair' IS allowed here, unlike the UK config: it is a real Australian label (reactive-clay soils make foundation movement a recognised residential problem) and it is the phrase the franchises use. 'reblocking' is kept as a separate value from 'restumping' even though it is the same job, because a Melbourne firm that calls itself a reblocker should be addressed as one — the mapping line makes restumping the default when a site uses both. 'subsidence repair' and 'resin injection' from the query list have no value of their own and land on foundation repair / underpinning respectively. 'damp proofing' and 'waterproofing' are banned outright: they are not this trade in Australia.
_r.inspection_type: The biggest Australian call in the file, and the inverse of the UK one: an Australian homeowner books an INSPECTION or an ASSESSMENT, never a survey ('survey' here means a land or building survey — a different profession). Using the UK 'surveys' wording is the clearest tell that the email was written for another market. 'free inspection' is the exact phrase the whole trade already advertises, so 'free' is banned outright (the engine also flags it as flag_free_in_visit). The per-trade table is chosen so that every row clears both live consistency flags: 'house levelling -> site assessments' (not 'levelling inspections', which would put 'levelling' in all three values), 'slab lifting -> concrete assessments' (not 'slab inspections' — keeps 'slab' to two values), 'underpinning' and 'house raising' both take 'site inspections' because neither trade noun reads as a visit.
_r.inspection_singular: Straight singular of the table value. It sits after 'a qualified, confirmed', so it has to be a single bookable thing — 'a qualified, confirmed subfloor inspection' reads; 'a qualified, confirmed restumping' does not.
_r.project_type: The outcome noun an Australian homeowner pays for. underpinning / restumping / reblocking are their own outcome nouns and read naturally before 'jobs' ('paid restumping jobs'). foundation repair takes 'repair' so that 'foundation' is not used three times. house levelling takes 'levelling'; slab lifting takes 'relevelling' (not 'lifting', which reads as a removalist, and not 'slab lifting', which would repeat the trade phrase). house raising takes 'house raising' — the only value where business_type and project_type are identical; WATCH THIS ONE in the 3-lead test ('paid house raising jobs' is what the trade says, but if the operator finds the repetition clumsy the candidate replacement is 'raising').
_r.city: Australian addresses carry suburb + state, and Maps hands back the suburb. For a metro business 'around Parramatta' is correct if the firm is a Parramatta business, but most capital-city foundation firms service the whole metro and would say 'around Sydney' — the instruction lets the reader choose the metro city when the site claims metro-wide service. Never the state ('around NSW' reads as an interstate agency wrote it) and never a region ('around South East Queensland'). WATCH THIS ONE: as in the UK, expect service-area listings with a blank city; read `blank_city` in fill_report.json BEFORE upload and clear it with `base --city-overrides` plus the engine's `city-fallback` sub-command (site re-read, keyless Nominatim, then the state's area name), both shipped 2026-09-17. `state` is kept in context_cols, unlike the UK config, because every Australian lead carries one and it helps the reader pick the right metro for a suburb name that exists in several states (there is a Richmond in NSW, VIC, QLD, SA and TAS).
_r.rules: Same two-part discipline as the UK rules line, stated against the flags the engine actually computes: flag_visit_repeats_trade, flag_word_used_3x, flag_free_in_visit and flag_outcome_off_trade. `redo` turns every flagged place_id into a higher-numbered batch whose values override on the next fill; loop fill -> redo -> one subagent -> fill until redo exits 2. The flags are the review — no eyeballing.
_r.outcome_by_type: Present from the FIRST fill, so flag_outcome_off_trade is live for this vertical from day one (build-plusvibe.js reads the table from the config since 2026-09-17; the UK run's first fill shipped with the flag silently inert). One allowed outcome noun per trade, matching the project_type instruction above exactly — if the instruction changes, this table changes with it.
_r.project_type_foundation_repair: 2026-09-21 3-lead test: 'paid repair jobs' read thin; operator chose the alternative -> 'rectification' ('foundation rectification' is the Australian trade term, and it keeps 'foundation' out of a third value, which 'paid foundation jobs' would have tripped as flag_word_used_3x).

_contact_name: OPERATOR NOTE — contact_name / salutation. Per the operator default, nothing here changes the name rule: a first and last name ride an address ONLY when the local part is built from that person's name (build-plusvibe.js `localOwns`; base writes name_basis=local_match, fill refuses to write on a violation, and `check --csv` re-applies it before upload). Role mailboxes — and this run will be mostly info@ / admin@ / enquiries@ — stay nameless whatever an upstream 'personal' tag says. A SEPARATE SALUTATION FALLBACK IS AN OPERATOR DECISION AND IS NOT SET HERE: the template opens with a bare 'Hi,' exactly as the US and UK ones do, and no {{first_name}} placeholder is introduced. Raise with the operator at the 3-lead test: (1) the engine's nickname table is US-shaped, so Australian short forms (Davo/David, Jono/Jonathan, Shaz/Sharon, Baz/Barry) do not resolve and those rows come out nameless — it fails safe, it does not mis-name; (2) first-name mailboxes (dave@, steve@) that the ranking scores below info@ are a ranking question for email-rank.js, not a name-rule question.
_test_plan: OPERATOR NOTE — the gated test sequence, per google-maps-scrape SKILL STEP 7b. NOTHING IS FILLED AT FULL VOLUME UNTIL BOTH TESTS ARE SIGNED OFF. (1) THREE-LEAD TEST: hand-pick 3 leads already on three different business_types — one underpinning, one restumping or reblocking (Victoria), one foundation repair or slab lifting (a franchise licensee is ideal) — run one subagent over a 3-item batch with skills/google-maps-scrape/personalize-subagent.md, and read the three finished `personalized_email` strings out loud to the operator. What is being checked is voice, not correctness: does 'site inspections' / 'subfloor inspections' / 'restumping jobs' sound like an Australian firm wrote it, and is 'paid house raising jobs' acceptable. (2) SEVEN-LEAD TEST: only after the 3-lead wording is agreed. Cover the remaining trades, include at least one house-raising (adjacent) lead, one brand-family licensee (Mainmark / Buildfix / Uretek), one lead with a blank city, one regional lead outside a capital, and one lead with no site text so the operator sees the fallback row as it will actually ship. Run `fill` on the 7 and read fill_report.json: expect 0 on all four flags (flag_outcome_off_trade is LIVE on this config). (3) FULL FILL: `prep` the rest, one Haiku subagent per batch, then fill -> redo -> subagent -> fill until `redo` exits 2, then `check --csv` on the finished upload. Report `fallback_only` and `blank_city` to the operator before any upload. Every correction the redo prompts produce is written back INTO THIS FILE'S per-trade tables.
